content.comment_body: Hello, I have my [product_name] connected to the cloud and made a webpage to monitor it. I have several timers and digital/analog inputs and outputs, and everything works online except for the weekly timer in my [product_name] program. On my [product_name], the timer is set for 10:00. In my AWS IoT shadow, I see the value for this variable as 1000, so that matches the timer being ON at 10:00. The issue is that on my webpage, the first digit (for the hours) appears as 16#10, and the second digit (for the minutes) as 16#0. I’m not sure why hexadecimal notation (#16) is showing before each digit. I’ve attached the [product_name] program, the [product_name] Web Editor configuration, and three screenshots. Does anyone know what I’m doing wrong?
I'm using [product_name] Web Editor v1.1.1 and [product_name] Soft Comfort V8.3.1.
Try using the scale time function instead of analog value input for time. Check the attached screenshot.
Great, it's working now! Thank you very much, [user_name].

analysis.insight_summary: The issue stemmed from a weekly timer value being displayed in hexadecimal format on the user's webpage, whereas the expected decimal format was shown in both the [product_name] device and the AWS IoT interface. The discrepancy was due to improper data formatting or scaling when integrating the [product_name] module with the cloud monitoring solution using [product_name] Web Editor. The problem was resolved by applying the correct time scaling method as suggested by another user.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants the weekly timer set in their [product_name] module to be displayed in a standard decimal format (matching the configured value) on both the cloud and web interfaces.
